picks.title: This new tool aims to identify and trace AI videos back to their source models
picks.headline: This new tool aims to identify and trace AI videos back to their source models
picks.excerpt: A UC Riverside team built SAGA (Source Attribution of Generative AI Videos), one of the first large-scale frameworks to trace an AI-generated clip back to the model that made it by reading the distinctive visual 'fingerprints' each generator leaves behind - a provenance tool with direct implications for deepfakes, rights and AI disclosure in filmmaking.
picks.rationale: First large-scale framework to attribute an AI clip back to its generator model — a fresh, actionable provenance tool for rights, disclosure and deepfake tracing. Not previously published in this section.

picks.title: NVIDIA tackles deepfakes and opens the door to AI agents at SIGGRAPH 2026
picks.headline: NVIDIA tackles deepfakes and opens the door to AI agents at SIGGRAPH 2026
picks.excerpt: At SIGGRAPH 2026 NVIDIA introduced a Synthetic Video Detector NIM microservice to help newsrooms and broadcasters flag AI-generated video, and showcased AI-agent integrations (via MCP) reaching into creative tools like Adobe and Unreal Engine - signalling how detection and agentic AI are entering the production and post pipeline.
picks.rationale: NVIDIA ships a Synthetic Video Detector microservice plus MCP agent hooks into Adobe/Unreal — a concrete detection + agentic shift for the post pipeline, from a distinct outlet. Not previously published in this section.
